reports.title: The Pentagon Chose Its AI Partners. Anthropic Said No.
reports.subtitle: Eight tech companies signed classified AI deals with the Defense Department. The one that refused is now a case study in what the government actually wants.

reports.title: The Administration That Doesn't Follow Court Orders
reports.subtitle: An AP review documents an unprecedented pattern: Trump officials defying lower court rulings not as exceptions but as policy.

reports.title: SCOTUS Guts the Voting Rights Act. Again.
reports.subtitle: A 6-3 ruling in the Louisiana redistricting case didn't kill Section 2 — it made compliance with Section 2 an unconstitutional act.

reports.title: Iran Offered a Deal. Trump Said No. The Blockade Continues.
reports.subtitle: Day 64 of the US-Iran war: a ceasefire holds in name while both sides blockade the world's most critical shipping strait and reject each other's terms.

reports.title: Trump Tears Up the Turnberry Agreement
reports.subtitle: Raising EU auto tariffs to 25% doesn't just hit cars. It breaches a deal that also covers semiconductors, AI chips, and digital trade — the things the US most needs from Europe right now.

reports.title: Trump Flies to Beijing. China Says Taiwan Is the Price of Admission.
reports.subtitle: Two weeks before the Trump-Xi summit, China's foreign minister told Rubio that Taiwan is the 'biggest risk' in the relationship — and the US side has not publicly disagreed.

reports.title: Trump Pulls Troops From Germany. Spain and Italy Are Next.
reports.subtitle: The withdrawal isn't about defense posture. It's punishment for not joining the Iran war, and every NATO ally knows it.

reports.title: Four Fed Officials Broke With Powell at His Last Meeting. That's the Story.
reports.subtitle: The biggest FOMC dissent since 1992 wasn't about rates. It was about whether the Fed can still pretend the next move is obviously a cut.

reports.title: Meta Threatens to Shut Down in New Mexico Rather Than Protect Kids
reports.subtitle: The trial starting Monday isn't about a fine. It's about whether a state court can order structural changes to a platform used by 2 billion people.

reports.title: Russia Lost Ground in April. Ukraine Is Striking Oil Refineries 1,600 Kilometers Deep.
reports.subtitle: For the first time since Ukraine's Kursk incursion, Russia suffered a net territorial loss in a single month. Whether it matters depends on why it happened.

reports.title: The $166 Billion Tariff Refund Nobody Asked For
reports.subtitle: The Supreme Court struck down Trump's tariffs. The refund goes to importers. The consumers who paid higher prices get nothing.

reports.title: The Dollar Is Down 10%. Nobody Agrees on What That Means.
reports.subtitle: A weaker dollar helps multinationals, hurts consumers, and is quietly accelerating a structural shift that America's foreign policy depends on stopping.

reports.title: Pakistan Staked Its Credibility on the Iran Deal. It Lost.
reports.subtitle: Army Chief Asim Munir flew to Tehran, hosted 21 hours of talks, and watched them collapse. The second round never happened. Iran just sent a new proposal anyway.

reports.title: Indonesia Just Made Roblox Scan Children's Faces. No Other Country Has Done This.
reports.subtitle: Under a new law called PP TUNAS, Roblox must verify the age of its 23 million Indonesian child users through facial recognition. It is the first country to extend age verification rules to gaming platforms.

reports.title: Northwestern Pays $75 Million. Harvard's Judge Says Antisemitism Was a Smokescreen.
reports.subtitle: Two universities, two opposite outcomes, same week. One court finds the funding freeze was political coercion. One university pays $75 million to end the investigation.

reports.title: AI Writes 80% of Code. Now What Happens to the People Who Used to?
reports.subtitle: OpenAI's president put a number on something everyone in tech already knew but wasn't saying: the software engineering workforce is being automated faster than any other profession in history.

reports.title: China Turned Airspace Into a Weapon. Taiwan Found a Workaround. The Tactic Survives.
reports.subtitle: Lai Ching-te reached Eswatini by borrowing the king's charter jet after China pressured multiple African countries to revoke overflight permits. The trip succeeded. The precedent is now set.

reports.title: China Just Made US Sanctions on Iran Unenforceable. Legally. In Writing.
reports.subtitle: Beijing issued a formal ban ordering Chinese companies not to comply with US sanctions on five Chinese refineries buying Iranian oil. This is not defiance through inaction. It is defiance by decree.

reports.title: The Democratic Party Has Broken on Israel. The Leadership Is Pretending Otherwise.
reports.subtitle: All but 7 Senate Democrats just voted to block weapons sales to Israel. The same week, the DNC blocked a floor vote on a resolution condemning AIPAC. Both facts are true at once.

reports.title: 57 Countries Declared the Fossil Fuel Era Over. The Same Week, Oil Spiked.
reports.subtitle: The Santa Marta summit was the most significant formal commitment to phasing out oil, gas, and coal in history. It met while the Strait of Hormuz blockade entered its tenth week and oil prices were rising, not falling.
